NNA-517.question: What proportion of people with sudden-onset neurological symptoms assessed by an ambulance crew have a validated FAST (Face Arm Speech Test) screen documented before hypoglycaemia is excluded and a stroke pre-alert decision is made?
NNA-517.pass: Both FAST score and capillary glucose recorded before the stroke pathway decision
NNA-517.change: Make both the FAST score and capillary glucose mandatory fields on the ambulance electronic patient report form before the stroke pre-alert option can be selected, so the sequence cannot be skipped.

NNA-518.question: What proportion of adults with major trauma and active or suspected bleeding who are taking an anticoagulant have a documented decision about reversal made with, or by, a haematologist?
NNA-518.pass: Reversal decision documented with haematology input, and no reversal without suspected bleeding
NNA-518.change: Add a mandatory 'anticoagulant reversal decision: haematology contacted, agent/reason' field to the trauma team clerking proforma whenever an anticoagulant is flagged in the drug history.

NNA-519.question: What proportion of adults triaged in the ED with a pain score of 7 or more (severe pain) receive their first analgesia within 20 minutes of triage?
NNA-519.pass: First analgesia given within 20 minutes of a pain score of 7 or more
NNA-519.change: Introduce a nurse-initiated analgesia protocol at triage for any adult scoring 7 or more, covering oral and intranasal options that do not need a doctor's prescription first.

NNA-520.question: What proportion of patients whose ambulance handover is delayed beyond 60 minutes have a full set of vital sign observations recorded by ambulance or ED staff at least every 30 minutes while still in the ambulance or queue?
NNA-520.pass: Full observations at least every 30 minutes, with escalation if NEWS2 rises
NNA-520.change: Introduce a joint ambulance-ED 'queue safety officer' role during any period when more than 2 ambulances are waiting, responsible for cycling through queued patients to check and escalate observations every 30 minutes.

NNA-521.question: In women on continuous CTG monitoring in labour, what proportion of hourly fetal heart rate assessments had an in-person 'fresh eyes' review by a second clinician documented before the next hourly assessment?
NNA-521.pass: Fresh-eyes review by a second clinician documented before the next hourly assessment
NNA-521.change: Add a timed 'fresh eyes review due at __:__' prompt to the CTG trace and electronic labour record that is generated automatically at each hourly assessment and must be signed by a second clinician before it can be marked complete.

NNA-522.question: In women with a low risk of complications having intermittent auscultation in established first stage of labour, what proportion of documented auscultations were performed at least once every 15 minutes?
NNA-522.pass: Auscultations no more than 15 minutes apart in established first stage
NNA-522.change: Build a 15-minute auscultation timer into the electronic partogram that flags amber when 12 minutes have elapsed since the last entry and red at 15 minutes, visible on the ward dashboard.

NNA-523.question: Once a woman has signs of, or is in confirmed second stage of labour, what proportion of documented intermittent auscultations were performed at least once every 5 minutes?
NNA-523.pass: Auscultations no more than 5 minutes apart in second stage
NNA-523.change: Add a distinct 'second stage' mode to the electronic partogram auscultation timer that shortens the alert interval from 15 to 5 minutes as soon as second stage is confirmed.

NNA-524.question: In women starting induction of labour, what proportion had a Bishop score and antenatal cardiotocography documented before the first method of induction was started?
NNA-524.pass: Bishop score and normal CTG documented before the first induction method
NNA-524.change: Redesign the induction of labour proforma so the Bishop score box and a mandatory pre-induction CTG result field must both be completed before the first prostaglandin, balloon or amniotomy step can be signed for.

NNA-525.question: In women having active management of the third stage after a vaginal birth, what proportion received the uterotonic at the correct dose and route (10 units oxytocin IM, 5 units oxytocin IV, or 5 units oxytocin plus 500 micrograms ergometrine IM)?
NNA-525.pass: One of the three NICE dose and route combinations given before cord clamping
NNA-525.change: Replace the third-stage drug chart pre-print with the three NICE-approved oxytocin/ergometrine dose-route options only, removing any legacy non-standard options.

NNA-526.question: In women with continuing postpartum haemorrhage who required a second-line uterotonic, what proportion also received intravenous tranexamic acid 1g given over 10 minutes?
NNA-526.pass: Tranexamic acid 1g IV over 10 minutes given alongside uterotonics
NNA-526.change: Add a pre-filled tranexamic acid 1g IV line to the maternity haemorrhage emergency box drug card and the PPH proforma, so it is prescribed at the same time as the second-line uterotonic.

NNA-527.question: In births with active management of the third stage, what proportion had the exact time of cord clamping recorded, and was the cord clamped no earlier than 1 minute and before 5 minutes from birth?
NNA-527.pass: Clamping time documented and done between 1 and 5 minutes after birth
NNA-527.change: Add a mandatory 'time of cord clamping' field, with an automatic timer started at the recorded time of birth, to the electronic birth record for every vaginal birth.

NNA-528.question: What proportion of babies had uninterrupted skin-to-skin contact with their mother (or birth companion if the mother was unable) started within 5 minutes of birth and continued for at least the first hour, with no separation for routine procedures during that time?
NNA-528.pass: Skin-to-skin starting within 5 minutes of birth and continuing uninterrupted for 1 hour
NNA-528.change: Add a 'skin-to-skin start and end time' box to the birth record and move routine weighing/measuring to after the first postnatal hour in the ward's standard birth checklist.

NNA-529.question: What proportion of babies had a parental decision about vitamin K prophylaxis (accepted by injection, accepted orally, or declined) recorded before transfer from the birth setting?
NNA-529.pass: Vitamin K decision recorded in the baby's notes before leaving the birth setting
NNA-529.change: Add a mandatory 'vitamin K discussed and decision recorded' field to the electronic newborn discharge checklist that must be completed before the birth episode can be closed.

NNA-530.question: What proportion of women who had an instrumental vaginal birth (forceps or ventouse) received a single dose of intravenous co-amoxiclav (or a locally agreed alternative) within 6 hours after cord clamping?
NNA-530.pass: Single IV co-amoxiclav dose given within 6 hours of cord clamping
NNA-530.change: Add a pre-filled 'co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV, single dose, within 6 hours of instrumental birth' order set to the electronic prescribing system, triggered when the birth mode is coded as forceps or ventouse.

NNA-531.question: What proportion of babies had a complete newborn and infant physical examination (NIPE) documented within 72 hours of birth?
NNA-531.pass: Complete newborn physical examination documented within 72 hours of birth
NNA-531.change: Add an automatic 'NIPE due by' countdown (birth time plus 72 hours) to the postnatal ward whiteboard/EPR task list, visible to the team booking discharges.

NNA-532.question: At each postnatal contact in the first 6-8 weeks, what proportion of women had their psychological and emotional wellbeing formally assessed and documented?
NNA-532.pass: Psychological wellbeing assessment recorded at each contact, with follow-up plan if concerns
NNA-532.change: Add a mandatory mood/emotional wellbeing assessment field to every postnatal contact template in the community electronic record, which must be completed before the contact can be closed.

NNA-533.question: What proportion of postnatal discharge records document that the baby had passed meconium within 24 hours of birth, or that a medical review was arranged if not?
NNA-533.pass: Meconium passed documented, or medical review sought before discharge
NNA-533.change: Add a mandatory 'meconium passed by 24 hours: yes/no/pending review' field to the electronic discharge checklist that must be completed before discharge is signed off.

NNA-534.question: What proportion of women had a documented venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk assessment at their antenatal booking appointment?
NNA-534.pass: Structured VTE risk assessment documented at the booking appointment
NNA-534.change: Make the structured VTE risk assessment tool a mandatory, non-skippable section of the electronic booking proforma.

NNA-535.question: What proportion of women having a vaginal birth had a systematic perineal examination, including a digital rectal examination, documented before perineal suturing?
NNA-535.pass: Systematic perineal examination including digital rectal examination documented before suturing
NNA-535.change: Redesign the perineal repair record as a structured proforma with a mandatory digital rectal examination tick box that must be completed before the suturing section can be signed.

NNA-536.question: Of instrumental vaginal births with a mediolateral episiotomy, what proportion had the episiotomy angle documented as approximately 60 degrees from the midline at the time of distension?
NNA-536.pass: Episiotomy angle of approximately 60 degrees documented at distension
NNA-536.change: Introduce an episiotomy angle guide (a single-use disposable protractor/angle indicator) at every instrumental birth, with a mandatory 'angle achieved' field on the instrumental birth proforma.

NNA-537.question: What proportion of women presenting with reduced fetal movements after 26 weeks had fetal heart rate auscultation, symphysis-fundal height/growth review and a fetal heart rate assessment (CTG) all completed and documented at that presentation, in line with the national RFM checklist?
NNA-537.pass: Heart rate auscultation, growth review and CTG all documented at the presentation
NNA-537.change: Introduce a structured RFM triage proforma based on the national Ask-Act-Advise checklist, with all three Act steps as mandatory fields before the assessment can be closed.

NNA-538.question: Of pregnant women identified as smokers and referred for tobacco dependence treatment, what proportion were contacted within 1 working day and seen face-to-face by a tobacco dependence adviser within 5 working days of referral?
NNA-538.pass: Contacted within 1 working day and seen face to face within 5 working days
NNA-538.change: Set up an automatic same-day electronic referral from the maternity CO-testing record straight into the tobacco dependence adviser's worklist, replacing any manual fax or paper referral step.

NNA-539.question: What proportion of women had a fetal growth restriction (FGR) risk assessment completed by 14 weeks' gestation, using a validated digital blood pressure monitor for the blood pressure component?
NNA-539.pass: FGR risk assessment completed by 14+0 weeks using a validated digital blood pressure monitor
NNA-539.change: Make the FGR risk assessment pathway a mandatory field in the electronic booking record with a due-date prompt at 14 weeks, and replace remaining manual sphygmomanometers in booking clinics with validated digital monitors.

NNA-540.question: What proportion of midwives and obstetricians providing intrapartum care had up-to-date annual training and competency assessment in intermittent auscultation and electronic fetal monitoring?
NNA-540.pass: Documented fetal monitoring training and competency assessment within the last 12 months
NNA-540.change: Set up an automatic training system alert to staff and their line manager 6 weeks before their fetal monitoring training expires, and block rostering onto the labour ward for staff more than 4 weeks overdue.

NNA-541.question: What proportion of women with pre-existing diabetes had an HbA1c measured at the start of the third trimester, with a documented increased-surveillance plan if the result was above 48 mmol/mol?
NNA-541.pass: HbA1c recorded at 28+0 to 28+6 weeks, with surveillance plan if above 48
NNA-541.change: Add an automatic HbA1c order and a due-date prompt at 28 weeks to the joint diabetes antenatal clinic pathway, with a mandatory 'surveillance plan' field triggered when the result exceeds 48 mmol/mol.

NNA-542.question: What proportion of babies born before 34 weeks' gestation had their first temperature recorded between 36.5 and 37.5 degrees Celsius, measured within one hour of birth?
NNA-542.pass: First temperature between 36.5 and 37.5 degrees, measured within 1 hour of birth
NNA-542.change: Introduce a preterm delivery normothermia bundle (pre-warmed delivery room, polythene wrap/hat, transwarmer mattress) as a standard checklist item for every birth under 34 weeks, based on the BAPM normothermia toolkit.

NNA-543.question: What proportion of babies born before 34 weeks' gestation received their own mother's milk within 24 hours of birth?
NNA-543.pass: Baby received own mother's milk within 24 hours, and expressing started within 2 hours
NNA-543.change: Ensure a breast pump, expressing consumables and written/verbal expressing support are available at the mother's bedside within 2 hours of a preterm birth, prompted by a checklist item on the neonatal admission pathway.

NNA-544.question: What proportion of women presenting with suspected pre-eclampsia between 20 and 36+6 weeks had placental growth factor (PlGF)-based testing performed as part of their assessment?
NNA-544.pass: PlGF-based testing performed at assessment, or reason for not performing recorded
NNA-544.change: Add PlGF-based testing as a default item on the suspected pre-eclampsia assessment order set in the maternal day assessment unit, alongside the standard bloods and urine protein tests.

NNA-545.question: Of women with pre-eclampsia who had given birth and remained on antihypertensive treatment, what proportion had their blood pressure kept below 140/90 mmHg before discharge from postnatal care?
NNA-545.pass: Last blood pressure before discharge below 140/90 mmHg, or ongoing management plan documented
NNA-545.change: Add a mandatory 'discharge blood pressure below 140/90, or plan documented' field to the postnatal discharge checklist for women coded with pre-eclampsia.

NNA-546.question: What proportion of women with a confirmed diagnosis of miscarriage were offered expectant management for 7 to 14 days as the first-line management strategy?
NNA-546.pass: Expectant management for 7-14 days offered before medical or surgical management
NNA-546.change: Redesign the early pregnancy unit miscarriage counselling proforma so expectant management is listed and discussed first, with a mandatory field recording why it was not chosen if applicable.

NNA-547.question: Of women with an ectopic pregnancy treated with systemic methotrexate, what proportion had serum hCG measured on days 4 and 7 after treatment, with weekly measurement continued until a negative result?
NNA-547.pass: hCG measured on days 4 and 7 after methotrexate, then weekly until negative
NNA-547.change: Give every woman starting methotrexate a pre-printed follow-up appointment card with day 4, day 7 and subsequent weekly hCG dates filled in at the time of treatment, and add the same schedule as a recall task in the early pregnancy unit tracking system.
